main_text.p: sed demùm in nepotibus adimpleri debuit oraculum Gen. ix. 27. Erit Canaan servus ejus, quia etiam Abraham Cananæam petiit, ut regionem exteram, remotam ab omni cognatione suâ & patriis sedibus, cessuram demùm posteris, minimè fanè pro avo ex parte subjectam; ne referam illud Suidæ aliorumque ex Veteribus, de Melchisedeco cœlibe, nec conjugato, quod alienum est à Semo. VI. Neque fidem merentur Arabes, Elmacinus, & Patricides, ἰσοφινῶς[?] citati ταλαίοις[?] nostro Hottingero, Collegæ Celeberrimo, & in novissimo Smegmate Orientali, Melchisedecum statuentes Pelegi filium. Quum & iisdem cum Semitis urgeantur incommodis; & commentum prodant annexæ fabulæ de Noachi Testamento, in quo declàm condendo Adami corpore, de ratione sacerdotij à Melchisedeco obeundi, de sacrificiis ex solo pane & vino &c. Omnia Siculis vaniora gerris. VII. Adeoque id unum supererit ut Melchisedek statuatur Salemensium Regulus (sive urbs illa Hierosolyma, ut Josephus, sive alia illa Job.

page.notes: The head "Epistolæ" is partly worn; the reading is uncertain. The Greek words after "citati" are hard to make out and are marked [?]. "declàm" is printed that way in the text ("de clàm"); it may be a misprint for "de clàm" or "declàm". Some letters at the line ends are blurred by ink spread (e.g. "Smegmate", "Elmacinus"). The bottom edge of the page carries a dark mark, which is not text.
